Private equity exit activity increased 36% year over year in 2025, with total exit value reaching its highest level in the past decade, excluding the exceptional conditions of 2021. Exit value as a percentage of NAV has lifted from the lows, but remains below long-term averages, with all asset classes still experiencing congestion from the 2021 period.
blocks.text: Private equity exit activity increased 36% year over year in 2025, with total exit value reaching its highest level in the past decade, excluding the exceptional conditions of 2021. Exit value as a percentage of NAV has lifted from the lows, but remains below long-term averages, with all asset classes still experiencing congestion from the 2021 period.

blocks.html: The increase in exit value was driven by strategic acquirors and mega-deals. The value of private equity exits to trade buyers increased approximately 83% year over year and exceeded 2021 levels, marking the largest year for corporate-led exits by value on record.1 While overall deal count has remained broadly stable, average transaction size has increased, indicating increased appetite from corporates toward larger, more strategic transactions to drive growth and enhance capabilities amid a more constrained organic environment.2

blocks.html: Our partner managers’ report increased engagement from strategic acquirers, with buyers demonstrating a greater willingness to transact at scale, despite ongoing macro and geopolitical volatility.3 Notable transactions across our GP partners included EnCap’s $4.1 billion sale of Double Eagle IV to Diamondback Energy,4 American Securities’ $8.8 billion sale of Foundation Building Materials to Lowe’s,5 and the announcement of ECP’s sale of Calpine to Constellation Energy for $26.6 billion- making it the most profitable private equity deal ever, by dollar value.6

blocks.html: IPO activity improved modestly in 2025, with a number of high-profile U.S. listings, including ICONIQ’s IPO of Chime and Platinum Equity’s listing of McGraw Hill.7 While IPOs remain an important indicator of public-market investor sentiment toward private assets, they contribute only modestly to overall exit value and liquidity.8 In 2026, liquidity may become more balanced across channels, particularly if certain slated “jumbo-listings” successfully come to market.9 However, with public markets structurally skewed towards larger offerings, we expect IPOs to remain a selective exit route for large, quality and more mature assets rather than a broad source of liquidity for private equity as a whole.

items: Stonepeak saw an approximate 17.9% increase in fair value, driven by the firm’s ongoing fundraising success, as well as the launch of its own private wealth vehicle, the Stonepeak+ Infrastructure Fund.
Similarly, Dragoneer was also marked up approximately 19.3%. The firm held a final close of Dragoneer Opportunities Fund VII at $4.3 billion, outpacing our expectations on both size and timing.
Lead Edge was marked up approximately 19.8%,as they held the final close of their seventh flagship fund at $3.5 billion commitments and continue to execute on their exit pipeline.
Growth Curve has also seen early success in the fundraise of their second flagship fund, leading to an approximately 20% increase in valuation.
Conversely, DivCore was marked down approximately 27% due to fundraising headwinds and the lower-than-expected underlying investment performance of their real estate portfolio.
Likewise, Bitkraft was marked down approximately 24% due to continued challenges in fundraising and harvesting of their funds.
Lastly, CVC saw an approximate 4.0% decrease driven by a decrease in the public stock price over the quarter and FX appreciation and PAI saw a half a basis point decrease driven by FX appreciation.

blocks.html: The HEC–Dow Jones 2025 Large Buyout Performance Rankings Methodology:
blocks.text: The HEC–Dow Jones 2025 Large Buyout Performance Rankings Methodology:

blocks.html: The HEC-Dow Jones Performance Rankings lists the world’s top PE firms in terms of aggregate performance. The method is able to aggregate performance across vintage years and considers relative and absolute returns. In total, the performance data from 695 PE firms and the 1,439 funds they raised between 2012 and 2021 with an aggregate equity volume of $2.5tn were analyzed. Firms were selected if they meet the criteria of at least two funds operating during the whole of the 10-year period. They are then selected for large-cap, mid-cap, small-cap and so on. PE firms with average performance have a score of 0. A score of one means a firm has an aggregate performance one standard deviation above the average, or better than roughly 85% of all firms assuming a Normal Distribution. A score of two means performance is twice as high as a firm that scores one in the sense that it positions a firm two standard deviations above the average.

blocks.html: The 2025 SecLink Awards Methodology:
Selection criteria:

Nominees and winners were determined through an open survey of industry professionals, distributed via SecondaryLink’s newsletter, LinkedIn channels, and direct outreach, with responses accepted only from professional work email addresses. Winners were determined by vote volume, with measures applied to limit coordinated or non-representative voting. There was no editorial involvement by the SecondaryLink team in the final results.

Where performance returns have been included in this material, Blue Owl has included herein important information relating to the calculation of these returns as well as other pertinent performance related definitions.The performance information displayed for certain funds managed by partner managers were selected on the basis of the three latest flagship fund vintages in their harvesting period and any subsequent flagship fund raised where Blue Owl is permitted to disclose such performance information. For these purposes, Blue Owl defines a fund’s “harvesting period” as the fund’s post-investment period before final liquidation and the "subsequent flagship fund raised" as any flagship fund that has held a final close and has begun collecting management fees, but is not yet in its harvesting period. Accordingly, in certain instances, a partner manager may have less than three flagship fund vintages which are in their harvesting period and in such instances only those flagship fund vintages, if any, which are in their harvesting period are displayed. Additionally, in certain instances, there may not be a subsequent flagship fund raised and the flagship fund vintages in their harvesting period are the latest funds to show. This performance information is being provided solely for discussion purposes to provide illustrative examples of flagship funds managed by the partner managers and does not reflect the performance of any Blue Owl Fund (as defined herein), or subset of investments of a Fund, managed by Blue Owl or its affiliates. For partner managers whose primary investments are hedge fund strategies, the flagship strategy is displayed.
